term: asserting, believing, knowing (Veracity vocabulary: Asserts, Believes, Knows)
definition: Asserts g p: g puts p forward as true on g's own word. Believes g p: g assents to p. Knows g p: g holds p as known. All three are uninterpreted parameters of the Veracity structure over the skeleton Signature. Factivity of knowing is NOT built in: that what a God with the classical attributes knows is true is the separate open premise STMT-GOD-KNOWS-ONLY-TRUTHS. Sincerity (asserting only what one knows) and infallibility (knowing only truths) are the two halves into which divine veracity (neither deceiving nor deceived) is split.
